deep.reconstruction:
This page is the sheet Gauss marked 'Litt. B'. The next page is 'Litt. C'. It continues the 1807 orbit computation of Vesta from four observations: 1807 Mar 30 Bremen, May 3 Milan, Jun 6 Bremen, Jul 11 Lilienthal. This is the worked example Gauss later printed in Theoria Motus (TM) II.4, arts. 164 ff., 'orbit from four observations of which only two are complete'. The previous page did observations I and II; this page does III (top block) and IV (middle block), then sets up the four-observation method (bottom block).

(A) SOLAR PLACES (solar tables of the von Zach type).

Observation III (Jun 6):
- Mean longitude: 9s9°42'23.9" + 5s3°45'39.5" + 55'5.8" = 2s14°23'9.2".
- Perigee: 9s9°36'17" + 26.6" = 9s9°36'43.6".
- Mean anomaly ≈ 5s4°46'25.6" (my subtraction).
- Equation of centre: +47'32.0". Further correction: +16.4".
- Perturbations: Moon 8.6, Venus 13.0, Mars 3.8, Jupiter 19.4, Saturn 0.3 (arcseconds); constant term −20.2".
- Total: 75°12'2.9" (I verified this sum).
- The radius-vector series (1.0151404 + 740 + 30 + 130 + 365 + 23) gives 1.0152692, so log R'' = 0.0065812.
- Columns M A B C D E F N are the arguments of the perturbation tables (the column sums are as transcribed).
- Obliquity: 23°27' + 53.4" − 3.35" − 0.60" = 23°27'49.45".

Observation IV (Jul 11):
- Mean longitude: 9s9°42'23.9" + 6s8°15'31.0" + 53'39.5" = 3s18°51'34.4".
- Perigee: 9s9°36'49.4". Mean anomaly = 6s9°14'45".
- Equation of centre: −18'55.1" (written as 11s29°41'4.9"). Further correction: +17.4".
- Perturbations: 14.6 + 19.2 + 4.0 + 17.1 + 0.1; constant term −20.2".
- Total: 108°34'11.9" (verified).
- Radius vector 1.0165799, so log R''' = 0.0071415.
- Obliquity: 23°27'49.2".

(B) PARALLAX AND COORDINATE CONVERSION.

Right-hand columns (parallax in right ascension and declination):
- Sidereal time plus offsets: 74°23'46" + 151°51'45" = 226°15'31". Minus RA 180°57'5" gives hour angle 45°18'26".
- Corrections for III: 2.14" in RA, 3.53" in Dec. Corrected place: α = 180°57'7.11", δ = 9°10'31.53".
- For IV: hour angle 83°11'49"; corrections 2.41" and 3.21". Corrected place: α = 189°49'10.11", δ = 3°9'13.31".

Equatorial to ecliptic (obliquity ε as above), with the standard formulas:
- sin β = sin δ cos ε − cos δ sin ε sin α
- tan λ = (sin α cos ε + tan δ sin ε) / cos α
- Gauss computes these through an auxiliary angle; the logs are in the middle columns.
- Results: III gives λ = 177°11'24.59", β = 8°47'21.82". IV gives λ = 187°46'23.05", β = 6°47'34.76". My recomputation confirms both to about 1".

(C) REDUCTION TO A COMMON EQUINOX.
- Constant corrections are subtracted from both the Earth's and the planet's longitudes: 25.65" for III and 31.45" for IV. The previous page's figures imply 16.97" for I and 20.68" for II.
- The increments match precession over the time intervals, so these are probably reductions to a common mean equinox. Both Earth and planet longitudes are reduced by the same amount.
- Earth heliocentric longitudes (l = Sun + 180°):
  - l = 189°21'17.97"
  - l' = 222°25'45.22"
  - l'' = 255°12'2.9" − 25.65" = 255°11'37.25"
  - l''' = 288°34'11.9" − 31.45" = 288°33'40.45"
- Geocentric longitudes:
  - α = 178°44'10.30"
  - α' = 173°34'41.25"
  - α'' = 177°11'24.59" − 25.65" = 177°10'58.94"
  - α''' = 187°45'51.60"
- Latitudes used: β' = 11°4'37.53" and β'' = 8°47'21.82". Only the middle two observations are complete.
- log R = 9.9998448, log R' = 0.0038571, log R'' = 0.0065812, log R''' = 0.0071415.
- Times from 1807 Mar 31.0 (Paris mean noon): t = −0.502164, t' = 33.355428, t'' = 67.431667, t''' = 102.407326 days.

(D) DIFFERENCES (all verified).
- Relative to α: l'−α = 43°41'34.92", α'−α = −5°9'29.05", α''−α = −1°33'11.36", l''−α = 76°27'26.95", l−α = 10°37'7.67".
- Right column, relative to α''': α'''−l'' = −67°25'45.65", α'''−α'' = 10°34'52.66", α'''−α' = 14°11'10.35", α'''−l' = −34°39'53.62", α'''−l''' = −100°47'48.85".
- An earlier attempt is struck out.

(E) PLANES SUN–EARTH–PLANET FOR OBSERVATIONS II AND III.
Each plane cuts the ecliptic along the Sun–Earth line, i.e. a node at longitude l' (or l'').
- Inclinations from tan i = tan β / sin(α − l):
  - α'−l' = −48°51'3.97", log sin = 9.8767962n, giving i' = 165°25'33.73".
  - α''−l'' = −78°0'38.31", log sin = 9.9904215n, giving i'' = 171°1'3.86".
- Arc u from the node to the observed place:
  - sin u = sin β / sin i
  - cos u = cos β cos(α − l)
  - II: log sin β' = 9.2835943, log sin i' = 9.4007617; log cos(α'−l') = 9.8182379, log cos β' = 9.9918326. Result u' = 49°46'38.63".
  - III: log sin β'' = 9.1841327, log sin i'' = 9.1934827; log cos = 9.3174992, log cos β'' = 9.9948698. Result u'' = 78°9'12.56".

(F) INTERSECTION OF THE TWO PLANES (Napier's analogies).
Spherical triangle on the ecliptic with side c = l''−l' and adjacent angles given by i', i''.
- Half-angles:
  - S = (i'+i'')/2 = 168°13'18.795"
  - D = (i''−i')/2 = 2°47'45.065"
  - c/2 = 16°22'56.015"
- Napier's analogies:
  - tan x = sin(c/2) sin S / (cos(c/2) sin D), giving x = 50°53'38.07".
  - tan y = sin(c/2) cos S / (cos(c/2) cos D), giving y = −16°4'24.25".
- Sides from the nodes to the line of intersection: x+y = 34°49'13.82" and x−y = 66°58'2.32".
- Delambre/Gauss: sin(C/2) = sin(c/2) sin S / sin x and cos(C/2) = cos(c/2) cos D / cos y. This gives C/2 = 4°15'17.26", so the mutual inclination is C = 8°30'34.51".
- On the next page these are combined with u', u'' (e.g. 34°49'13.82" − 49°46'38.63" = −14°57'24.81").

(G) TIME QUANTITIES (k = 0.01720209895, log k = 8.2355814).
- Intervals: t'−t = 33.857592, t''−t' = 34.076239, t'''−t'' = 34.975659.
- Logs: 1.5296561, 1.5324516, 1.5437658. Adding log k gives log θ = 9.7652375, 9.7680330, 9.7793472.
- First approximations:
  - P' = (t''−t')/(t'−t), log 0.0027955
  - P'' = (t''−t')/(t'''−t''), log 9.9886858
  - Q' = ½k²(t'−t)(t''−t'), log 9.2322405
  - Q'' = ½k²(t''−t')(t'''−t''), log 9.2463502
- Total interval 102.90949 days (written 102°90949). log 2.0124554½; log kT = 0.2480369.

(H) COEFFICIENTS OF THE FINAL EQUATIONS.
- log a' = 9.8866896, log a'' = 9.9972313, b' = −8.5509454, b'' = −5.3744895.
- How they derive from the angles above is not shown on this page. The next page solves x' ≈ 2.0979, x'' ≈ 1.9736 and iterates P, Q.
errors: No genuine computational errors found; every sum, difference and log combination I checked is consistent.

log cos(48°51'3.97") is 9.8182379. The transcribed 9.8181379 is off by 1e-4, but Gauss's next step (9.8100705 = 9.8182379 + 9.9918326) uses the correct value, so this is a reading or overwriting issue rather than a slip.
Gauss's later recomputation shows 9.8866898 on the next page versus 9.8866896 here for log a'. This is a last-digit discrepancy.
Rounding: the parallax and coordinate conversions agree with my recomputation to about 1"; no material discrepancy.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the working draft of the published Vesta four-observation example in Theoria Motus; the methods and numbers are Gauss's known published material. Its value is as a record of his computational practice (reductions, checks, iteration) rather than new mathematics.

transcription_corrections: Heading reads 'Litt. B.' (followed by a small number), not 'Lilit. [?]'; the next page is 'Litt. C.'
'9,8181379' should be 9,8182379 (log cos 48°51'3.97"); Gauss's next value 9.8100705 confirms this.
'5. 4. 46. 43' (mean anomaly III) is probably 5.4.46.25,6 per the arithmetic; uncertain reading.
'Tempus 102° 90949' means 102.90949 days (t''' − t), whose log is 2.0124554½.
'51. 236. 802. 633 645...' is the row of perturbation-table arguments M A B C D E F N for IV (e.g. 51/236/802/633/645/862/598/312); the leading figure is uncertain.
The marginal '25,65' and '31,45' are equinox/reduction corrections subtracted from λ and from the solar longitude + 180°, not stray numbers.
